name: DinnerDateDisaster
source:
`` I do n't believe this,'' she said. 
 
 `` Swear to god it's the truth,'' he said, struggling to get the distinctive stain off of his dinner jacket. `` Hm, maybe I can ask the waiter for some lemon juice from the kitchen? I hear lemon juice is good for stains.'' 
 
 She allowed her head to fall, slowly, to the table. She supposed it was her own fault for agreeing to go on a date with *him. * Everyone knew about the bizarre things that happened to and around him, as though he was a magnet for the strange. 
 
 `` I promise, it was n't my fault.'' 
 
 `` I believe you, it's just... could you at least have taken a few moments to get the pseudopods out of your hair?'' 
 
 He brushed a rubbery tendril out. `` Sorry, I thought you'd want me to get here as soon as possible.'' 
 
 She sighed again. `` You were already an hour late, another ten minutes to shower and change would n't have made that big of a difference.'' 
 
 `` Yes, well, ten minutes and something even harder to clean up might've happened. Like, if I had been set on by a herd of octopodes, you know how hard it is to get the slime out.'' 
 
 She began rhythmically beating her head against the table. The worst part? She *did* know.
retelling:
Narrated by He:

In this tale, I, the enigmatic He, found myself seated across from She, a woman as captivating as she was perplexed by my peculiarities. We were ensconced in a restaurant, an environment where the clink of cutlery and hum of conversation served as our soundtrack.

The evening began auspiciously enough, but then I arrived late - not because I intended to, but due to an encounter with some rather unusual octopi. I chose to delay my arrival, believing it would ensure a smoother night for both of us. Little did She know that had I arrived on time, our date might have taken a turn for the worse.

Upon entering, I noticed something amiss - there was a stain on my dinner jacket and pseudopods adorning my hair. It appeared that during my fateful encounter with the octopi, they'd left behind more than just memories. I tried to explain this unforeseen mishap to She, hoping she would understand.

However, instead of compassion or intrigue, I met only exasperation and frustration. Yet, I couldn't help but marvel at the irony: here we were, two individuals bound by an unusual connection, yet struggling to find common ground amidst our unique experiences.
